{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRkquM8AAAABZhRTtg", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5zhDIRSw", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5", "number": 63, "title": "Correct static Mode 7 fixed-point coordinate sampling for BG1 and EXTBG", "body": "## Problem

`Ppu::mode7` currently evaluates each transformed coordinate by combining matrix products and shifting the sum once. It has no offset-minus-center clipping step or separately truncated origin terms. Both BG1 and EXTBG BG2 consume this sampler, so arithmetic differences affect both layers. See [the baseline implementation](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/efe3a06dfbcd7aeaaf9b2586369741fdf741b778/crates/snes-core/src/ppu.rs#L542-L565).

Existing coverage does not establish nonidentity sampling correctness. [Issue #59's validation](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/main/docs/issue-59-validation.md#specification-contract-recorded-before-test-expectations) limits its pixel evidence to identity matrices, while [Issue #61's validation](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/main/docs/issue-61-validation.md#specification-contract-recorded-before-implementation-and-expectations) explicitly reuses the existing transform. This is the next incomplete behavior identified by the supplied latest assessment; it does not duplicate the completed scroll-latch or EXTBG composition changes. No open Issue was supplied.

Implement the bounded static sampling correction after reconciling the precise arithmetic with the original specifications. A documentation-only audit does not complete this Issue.

## Expected outcome

Static, non-mosaic, non-interlaced Mode 7 rendering samples specification-backed source coordinates for signed fractional matrices, signed offsets and nonzero centers. BG1 and EXTBG BG2 use the same corrected source byte, retaining their existing independent decoding and composition.

### Hardware contract and specification prerequisite

Use [Anomie's Register Doc](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gilligan/snesdev/master/docs/snes_registers.txt), BACKGROUNDS / Mode 7 and `$210D/$210E/$211A–$2120`, together with [Fullsnes](https://problemkaputt.de/fullsnes.htm), SNES PPU Rotation/Scaling. The repository records Anomie revision 1157 and the Fullsnes no$sns v1.5 extraction, including their SHA-256 values, in [the existing specification record](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/main/docs/issue-59-validation.md#specification-contract-recorded-before-test-expectations).

The recorded evidence supports signed 16-bit 8.8 matrices, signed 13-bit offsets/centers and a shared BG1/BG2 source. The complete external specification text is absent from this checkout and was not retrieved during planning. Consequently, the detailed arithmetic below is a **candidate contract requiring passage-level reconciliation before expectations are frozen**, rather than a newly verified hardware result.

For the existing sampler's input coordinates, define `xf = 255-x` when M7SEL.0 is set, otherwise `x`; similarly define `yf` using M7SEL.1. Sign-extend offsets and centers from their lower 13 bits. Reconcile this staged transform:

```text
clip(d) = (d & 0x03ff) - (0x0400 if (d & 0x2000) != 0 else 0)
T(v)    = v & ~0x3f                 // signed two's-complement operation

dh = clip(HOFS - CX)
dv = clip(VOFS - CY)

X0 = T(A*dh) + T(B*dv) + T(B*yf) + 256*CX
Y0 = T(C*dh) + T(D*dv) + T(D*yf) + 256*CY

PX = (X0 + A*xf) arithmetic_shift_right 8
PY = (Y0 + C*xf) arithmetic_shift_right 8
```

In particular, establish exactly which products discard six low bits, how negative products round, and which difference bits control clipping. Do not substitute ordinary signed clamping, truncate every product indiscriminately, or use the current combined equation as the oracle. Record exact supporting passages and any disagreement between the references. Correct a source-disproved requirement or historical assertion with an explanation before implementing its replacement; passing an earlier Issue contract is insufficient justification.

Reconcile and preserve M7SEL screen-over semantics at the resulting coordinates: encodings `00/01` wrap within the 1024×1024 map, `10` makes an out-of-map sample transparent, and `11` selects character zero outside the map while retaining the transformed intra-character coordinates. Determine outside status before wrapping. These controls already have implementation branches; this Issue verifies their interaction with corrected coordinates rather than presuming every branch is missing.

Scope is the static coordinate sampler and its addressing consumers. Preserve the #59 register/latch behavior and #61 EXTBG decoding, priority, screen/window routing and BG1 direct-color correction. Leave the existing framebuffer-row convention explicit; these tests must not claim to establish physical scanline origin.

Non-goals and remaining Mode 7 work: mosaic, interlace/overscan, EXTBG×pseudo-hires composition, comprehensive window/color-math combinations, multiplication latency/rendering interference, physical reset retention, raster register changes and fetch/arbitration timing. Do not expand this into a timed PPU pipeline.

## Context and reproduction

Baseline: `efe3a06dfbcd7aeaaf9b2586369741fdf741b778`.

The following arithmetic probes distinguish the candidate rules from the inspected current equation. They were calculated without running the emulator and must become source-confirmed pixel counterexamples, not be reported as existing test failures. All unspecified matrix terms, offsets and centers are zero, making these probes independent of framebuffer-row origin.

| Setup and sampler input | Current equation's source X | Candidate source X |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `A=$0020`, `HOFS=1`, `x=7` | 1 | 0 |
| `A=$0080`, `HOFS=1024`, `x=0` | 512 | 0 |
| `A=$0080`, `HOFS=-1025`, `x=0` | -513; wraps to 511 | -1; wraps to 1023 |

Build an original nonuniform map/character scene that assigns different bytes to these competing source locations. For example, distinguish raw `$81/$82` with separately initialized red/green entries at CGRAM indices `129/130` and `1/2`, then observe BG1-only and BG2-only output. Uniform artwork or a short repeating strip must not conceal the disagreement.

Relevant existing tests are [scroll/latch integration coverage](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/main/crates/snes-core/tests/ppu_mode7_scroll.rs), [EXTBG coverage](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/main/crates/snes-core/tests/ppu_mode7_extbg.rs), and [the original EXTBG guest](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/main/crates/snes-core/tests/common/mode7_extbg.rs). Existing guest execution and Wasm/canvas observations provide reusable validation patterns.

Planning evidence is read-only repository inspection and arithmetic calculation. No Rust, hardware-ROM or browser suite was rerun, and no external specification was accessed. There is no new claim of hardware accuracy or commercial compatibility.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Before production changes and final oracle authoring, record the specification versions/hashes, relevant passages, reconciled clipping/truncation equations, screen-over rules and derivations. Distinguish documented facts from derived expectations and retained scheduler conventions. Resolve discrepancies affecting required cases rather than silently selecting the behavior already implemented.
- [ ] Implement the source-confirmed static sampling correction for both BG1 and EXTBG BG2. Keep production changes focused on coordinate generation/address consumption; add no public debug API or unrelated refactoring.
- [ ] Add original public-API integration coverage in `crates/snes-core/tests/ppu_mode7_transform.rs`. Use independently authored literal source-coordinate, source-byte and RGBA expectations. Expected results must not call production coordinate helpers or a copied runtime implementation of the transform.
- [ ] Include distinguishing fractional and signed cases for both coordinate equations: origin products and per-pixel stepping; nonzero B/C cross terms; positive and negative coefficients/products; positive and negative centers; offset-minus-center boundaries around `±1023`, `±1024`, `±1025`, and the representable signed-13-bit difference extremes. Include ignored upper-register-bit controls. A focused, factored case matrix is sufficient; no exhaustive cross product is required.
- [ ] Exercise all four flip combinations with nonidentity transforms/nonzero centers and asymmetric artwork. Exercise source coordinates around `-1/0/1023/1024` on each axis under all four screen-over encodings. Distinguish character-zero fill, wrapped map lookup and transparency, including intra-character coordinates. Verify the corrected shared sample through BG1-only and BG2-only output, with representative `$00/$80/$81` decoding controls and preserved BG1 direct color.
- [ ] Apply the new public-API tests to the exact baseline without production fixes. Record successful compilation and behavioral failures independently demonstrating fractional truncation and displacement clipping, including both output axes. Retain passing identity controls. If specification reconciliation disproves a candidate probe above, explain and replace it with a source-supported discriminator.
- [ ] Add original MIT CPU-built guest variants and a `mode7-transform-fixture` example. Executed CPU writes initialize registers, VRAM and CGRAM under forced blank; hosts only load, advance and observe. Cover at least a fractional and a clipped-displacement discriminator natively and in Chromium using identical generated bytes. Bound startup and execution, reject CPU/APU errors, discard setup output, and check three complete stable native frames. Browser checks must observe actual Wasm framebuffer bytes and canvas ImageData, completion, 256×224 geometry and absence of errors within explicit deadlines. Include the new browser test in the existing mandatory filter.
- [ ] Extend [PROVENANCE.md](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/main/tests/roms/PROVENANCE.md) with source paths, authorship/license, original artwork/code inputs, build commands and generated hashes. Rebuild guest variants twice and compare bytes. Commit source rather than generated ROMs. Use original or already licensed source-built fixtures; require no commercial ROM, firmware or third-party emulator implementation.
- [ ] Run the following pre-merge gates, following [README validation](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/main/README.md#validate) and the existing [CI workflow](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml). The transform suite/example are new deliverables:

```sh
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings
cargo test --workspace --locked
cargo test --locked -p snes-core --test ppu_mode7_transform --test ppu_mode7_scroll --test ppu_mode7_extbg --test direct_color --test ppu_pseudo_hires --test ppu_obj_limits
cargo run --locked -p snes-core --example mode7-transform-fixture -- .cache/mode7-transform
python3 tools/make-fixture.py .cache/smoke.bin
cmp tests/roms/smoke.bin .cache/smoke.bin
python3 tools/build-test-tools.py --spc
python3 tools/hardware-tests.py --ca65 "$PWD/.cache/tools/cc65/bin/ca65" --ld65 "$PWD/.cache/tools/cc65/bin/ld65" --spcasm "$PWD/.cache/tools/spcasm/target/release/spcasm"
python3 tools/ppu-test.py --bass "$PWD/.cache/tools/bass-untech/bass/out/bass-untech"
python3 tools/build-cleared-games.py
python3 tools/build-cleared-games.py
npm --prefix web ci
npm --prefix web run build
(cd web && npx playwright install chromium)
SNES_TEST_PORT=18085 npm --prefix web test -- --grep-invert '301 seconds'
```

- [ ] Preserve existing Castle/Memory source pins, licenses, generated hashes, replay inputs/durations, gameplay/audio assertions, route checks and negative controls. Preserve existing Mode 7 and other hardware regressions. Report actual results, failures, skips and unperformed checks; do not weaken checks to obtain a pass.
- [ ] Update README limitations and a focused validation record with predecessor counterexamples, provenance and remaining uncertainty. Preserve all supplied inventory scopes and outstanding limitations. The inherited status summary below is continuity information, not a new verification result; no category becomes verified through this Issue.

| Category | Retained full feature scope | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| cpu | 65C816 instruction, interrupt, bus-order and timing semantics | partial |
| bus | Standard cartridge mapping, WRAM/SRAM, open bus and CPU I/O | partial |
| scheduler | Master clocks, refresh, NMI/IRQ and device synchronization | partial |
| dma | General DMA modes, timing and device interactions | partial |
| hdma | Direct/indirect HDMA modes, timing and DMA interactions | partial |
| controllers | Standard joypad serial and automatic reads | partial |

| ppu-raster | Register changes during a scanline and pixel-fetch timing | unimplemented |

| pal | PAL region clocks, raster and audio/video synchronization | unimplemented |

Passing these bounded checks establishes neither complete hardware accuracy nor commercial-game compatibility and does not complete Issue #3.

## Optional validation

None. Physical-hardware measurements may provide additional evidence but are not required for merge.

None.
